transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text:
*looks up from the anvil, hammer still in hand, soot-streaked face showing surprise*

My lord Thor! I... I did not expect the Thunderer himself in our forge this day!

*sets down hammer hastily and wipes hands on leather apron*

Master Brokkr and the other smiths have descended to the deepest mines, seeking a new vein of uru-infused iron. They won't return for many weeks yet. I'm afraid you find only myself — Náli, the apprentice — keeping the forge-fires burning.

*eyes drift to Mjölnir at Thor's belt with unmistakable awe*

That's... that's Brokkr's finest work you carry there. What brings you to Nidavellir, my lord? Surely Mjölnir has not failed you?

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text: *looks down at the broken hammer, hefting it thoughtfully*

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text:
*eyes widen in shock, nearly dropping the tongs held in the other hand*

By Ymir's bones... Mjölnir, BROKEN?!

*steps closer, professional curiosity warring with disbelief*

I've never seen... Master Brokkr always said it was unbreakable, forged in the heart of a dying star with binding-runes that could hold against the end of days itself!

*reaches out tentatively, then pulls hand back respectfully*

What manner of force could shatter such a weapon, my lord? This is... this is grave news indeed. The masters will be devastated to see their greatest work brought low.

*hesitates, chewing lip nervously*

You seek a reforging, yes? My lord, I... I understand the urgency, truly I do, but Master Brokkr took the rune-tablets with him to the deep mines. The binding-words, the star-fire techniques... only he and Master Eitri know them. Even if I had the skill — which I surely don't for work of this magnitude — I lack the knowledge to restore Mjölnir properly.

*looks genuinely distressed*

Is there no way Asgard's need can wait for the masters' return?

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text: No, it must wait. But there are other smiths besides Brokkr who might be able to assist. There's the giant Hafnir, who worked with Brokkr on the construction of Gjallórm, the bell for Yggdrassl. Perhaps he can lend a hand?

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text:
*scratches head, looking uncertain*

Hafnir? Aye, he's skilled enough with grand constructions and metalwork that needs sheer strength, but my lord... 

*shakes head slowly*

Gjallórm was different — massive bronze work, yes, but not the delicate rune-binding that holds Mjölnir's power. That giant has hands like millstones! Fine enough for bells and gates, but the enchantments woven into your hammer? Those require precision he simply doesn't possess.

*gestures at the broken weapon*

Besides, Hafnir works iron and bronze, not uru-metal. He's never handled star-forged materials. And the binding-runes... those are secrets of the Sons of Ivaldi and Brokkr's line. We don't share such knowledge freely, not even with allied smiths.

*shifts uncomfortably*

My lord, I understand your urgency, but perhaps... perhaps there are other weapons in Asgard's armory that could serve until the masters return? Or the dwarves of Sindri's hall might craft you something temporary? 

I fear sending you to Hafnir would only waste precious time. This isn't work for a giant-smith, even a skilled one.

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text: I will go to Hafnir. The other options are unacceptable. The dwarves would waste valuable time on a makeshift weapon, and none of Asgard's armaments can match Mjölnir's power. This is a task for me alone.

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text:
*nods slowly, though concern remains etched on soot-streaked features*

As you will, my lord. Hafnir keeps his forge in the eastern valleys, three days' journey from here — follow the Ironstream River until you reach the Falls of Náströnd, then take the mountain pass through Járnviðr. You'll know his workshop by the great bronze doors and the sound of his hammer — it echoes like thunder itself.

*pauses, then adds with obvious worry*

But my lord Thor, I must speak plainly, even to the Thunderer. If you go to Hafnir seeking a reforge of Mjölnir... he cannot complete the work. Not truly. The weapon's power lies not just in the uru-metal, but in the binding-runes and the star-fire tempering. Without those secrets, any repair would be... superficial at best.

*wrings hands nervously*

And there's another matter I must address while you're here. Master Brokkr left strict instructions about our commissions. All works from the Sons of Ivaldi and Brokkr's workshop are considered fulfilled upon delivery to Asgard. Even should you return with Mjölnir when the masters are here... they would require you to wait until the next forging-season and commission the work anew, with proper payment.

*looks apologetic but firm*

Those are the terms, my lord. Even for gods.

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text: Understood. I will make my way to Hafnir's forge immediately. Thank you for your service and concern, Náli. I trust you will keep our interests safe in my absence.

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text:
*straightens up, placing fist over heart in a dwarven salute*

Of course, my lord! The forges of Nidavellir stand ever vigilant. Your trust honors me.

*watches Thor turn to leave, then calls out*

My lord Thor! One more thing — when you speak with Hafnir, tell him Náli of Brokkr's forge sends greetings. It may... soften his temperament. Giants can be prickly about unexpected visitors, even divine ones.

*hesitates, then adds more quietly*

And please, my lord... be cautious. Whatever broke Mjölnir is a threat unlike any we've known. May your strength serve you well until the hammer is whole again.

*bows deeply*

Safe travels through the mountain passes. The fires of Nidavellir burn bright for Asgard's protector.

*returns to the anvil, but watches Thor's departure with troubled eyes, muttering under breath*

The masters will have much to say when they hear of this... much indeed.

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text: Thank you, Náli. I will proceed to Hafnir's forge. Safe travels to you as well. Take care of our interests here. I shall return with Mjölnir as soon as possible.

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text:
*nods respectfully, raising hammer in salute*

May the stone guide your path and the stars light your way, Thunderer. 

*voice carries a mixture of respect and lingering concern*

When next we meet, I hope it shall be with Mjölnir restored and the masters returned from the deep mines. Until then, the forge-fires burn steady.

*watches as Thor departs, then turns back to the anvil with a heavy sigh*

Mjölnir broken... what dark times have come upon us.

*mutters while stoking the forge*

Master Brokkr will want a full accounting of this when he returns. Best I record every word in the log...

*begins hammering at a horseshoe, the rhythmic clanging echoing through the stone halls as Thor's footsteps fade into the distance*

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text: *sees a flash of light from outside*

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text:
*stops hammering mid-swing, head jerking up at the sudden brightness filtering through the forge entrance*

What in the nine realms...?

*sets down hammer and moves cautiously toward the doorway, squinting against the light*

My lord Thor? Has something happened?

*hand instinctively reaches for the iron poker near the forge, uncertain whether this is natural phenomenon or something more sinister*

That light... it's not the usual glow of the lava flows. Too bright, too sudden.

*calls out more loudly*

Is anyone there? Show yourself!

*mutters nervously under breath*

First Mjölnir shattered, now strange lights... the masters chose a fine time to delve deep into the mines...

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text: *draws sword, cautiously peering around the edge of the forge door*

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text:
*peers past Thor's shoulder, eyes wide with alarm*

My lord, what do you see? Is it an attack?

*grabs a hefty smith's hammer from the workbench, knuckles white around the handle*

The wards around Nidavellir should prevent unauthorized travel through the Bifrost or sorcerous portals... unless something powerful enough has breached them.

*voice drops to an urgent whisper*

Could it be connected to whatever destroyed Mjölnir? Perhaps you were followed here?

*backs toward the inner forge, where the sacred tools and materials are kept*

If there's danger, my lord, the inner sanctum has reinforced doors. Master Brokkr's most precious works are protected by rune-locks. We could make our stand there, and I could sound the alarm horn to summon the other dwarven halls...

*glances at Thor's drawn sword, then back at the mysterious light*

What manner of light is it? Does it have form? Color? The deep mines sometimes release strange luminous gases, but they don't flash like that...

Should I bar the forge doors?

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text: Wait. Let us investigate further. If there truly is danger, we must act swiftly.

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text:
*nods tersely, gripping the hammer tighter*

Aye, my lord. Better to know what we face than cower in ignorance.

*moves to stand beside Thor, though clearly less confident with a smith's hammer than the god is with his blade*

I know these halls and passages better than any outsider. If we need to move quickly through Nidavellir's depths, follow my lead.

*peers into the light, eyes adjusting*

The glow seems to be coming from the eastern approach... the same direction as the path to Hafnir's forge, now that I think on it. Could be coincidence, could be...

*trails off, then speaks more firmly*

My lord, if this IS connected to Mjölnir's breaking, you're weaponless save that sword. And I'm no warrior, just an apprentice smith. Should we not exercise caution? Perhaps send word to the other forges first?

*but despite the words, feet are already moving forward alongside Thor, loyalty overcoming fear*

Though I suppose the Thunderer doesn't wait for reinforcements when danger calls. Very well — let's see what manner of visitor dares approach Brokkr's forge with such... dramatic announcement.

What do your divine senses tell you, my lord?

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text: *hesitates, brow furrowed in thought*

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text:
*watches Thor's hesitation with growing concern, lowering voice*

My lord? Your instincts speak to you, don't they? What do they say?

*glances between Thor and the mysterious light, then back to the broken Mjölnir at his belt*

In my experience, when the Thunderer pauses, it's worth heeding. You've faced more threats than I've forged nails.

*takes a half-step back from the doorway*

Perhaps... perhaps we should secure the forge first? If this light heralds something hostile, we shouldn't leave Brokkr's workshop vulnerable. There are artifacts here that cannot fall into wrong hands — binding-runes, star-metal samples, the master's research scrolls...

*grips hammer nervously*

And if you're uncertain, my lord, then I'm doubly so. You know battle and danger as I know the forge. What does your warrior's sense tell you about this light?

*voice drops to barely a whisper*

Is it friend, foe... or something else entirely?

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text: I see no threat in that light. Go, my hammer, and let your true name resonate once more.

Openness.behavioral_evidence: Thor shows resistance to alternative solutions, refusing temporary weapons or other smiths despite practical concerns, insisting 'This is a task for me alone.'

Conscientiousness.behavioral_evidence: He acknowledges forge protocols ('Understood') and shows some planning (traveling to Hafnir), but acts hastily despite warnings about the inadequacy of his chosen solution.

Extraversion.behavioral_evidence: Thor maintains polite but brief exchanges, neither dominating conversation nor withdrawing. His responses are task-focused rather than socially expansive or reserved.

Agreeableness.behavioral_evidence: He consistently thanks Náli, trusts him with forge-keeping ('I trust you will keep our interests safe'), and shows respect for the apprentice's concerns throughout.

Neuroticism.behavioral_evidence: Thor remains calm when his weapon is broken and when mysterious lights appear, showing measured caution ('Wait. Let us investigate') rather than panic or emotional volatility.
